--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[PAY-1] Client-trusted prices allow underpayment
File: src/app/api/checkout/create-order/route.ts (L1-L220), src/app/api/checkout/razorpay-order/route.ts (L1-L120), src/app/checkout/page.tsx (L1-L220)
Evidence: The client calculates item prices/total and sends them to /api/checkout/create-order and then the frontend sends the client-calculated amount to /api/checkout/razorpay-order; the server accepts the amount and creates a Razorpay order using the client-provided amount without validating it against the DB-stored product prices/order total. This lets a malicious client reduce prices/total or craft a smaller amount to be charged.  
Impact: Attackers can pay less than the real order value, resulting in direct revenue loss and invalid accounting under production traffic.  
Fix: Compute and assert totals server-side (recalculate item prices and shipping/coupons from DB) and require razorpay-order creation only with the server-validated order total; reject mismatches.

[PAY-2] Webhook processing is not idempotent (duplicate shipments/charges)
File: src/app/api/webhooks/razorpay/route.ts (L1-L300)
Evidence: The Razorpay webhook verifies signature but does not persist the webhook/event id or otherwise deduplicate events; it unconditionally attempts Shiprocket order creation on every captured event and only logs failures (no dedupe guard).  
Impact: Retries or duplicate webhook deliveries can create duplicate Shiprocket orders/shipments and produce duplicate shipping charges or double-fulfillment (real revenue & fulfillment loss).  
Fix: Persist the provider event ID and enforce a unique constraint / check before processing (or enqueue a deduped background job) so each webhook is processed exactly once.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[PAY-3] Order matching uses orderNumber instead of razorpayOrderId
File: src/app/api/webhooks/razorpay/route.ts (L120-L200), prisma/schema.prisma (Order model)
Evidence: The webhook looks up orders by orderNumber === payment.order_id, while the schema also contains dedicated razorpayOrderId/razorpayPaymentId fields and other routes store Razorpay IDs inconsistently (razorpay-order writes to orderNumber).  
Impact: If the Razorpay ID isn't reliably written to orderNumber (or flows diverge), webhooks may fail to find paid orders and leave them unconfirmed, causing paid-but-unfulfilled orders.  
Fix: Use a dedicated razorpayOrderId column for provider IDs and have all paths populate it; change webhook lookup to search by razorpayOrderId with sensible fallbacks.

[PAY-4] Coupon decrement not atomic with order creation
File: src/app/api/checkout/create-order/route.ts (L40-L120)
Evidence: The code decrements coupon.quantity before creating the Order and does not wrap coupon decrement + order creation in a single transaction or rollback path.  
Impact: If order creation fails after coupon decrement (or concurrent requests race), coupon quantity can be lost and discounts overconsumed, causing revenue leakage.  
Fix: Decrement coupon quantity inside the same DB transaction that creates the order (or use a DB-level counter constraint) so both succeed or both roll back.

--- INFO ---

[PAY-5] Server-side Razorpay signature verification present
File: src/app/api/checkout/verify-payment/route.ts and src/app/api/webhooks/razorpay/route.ts
Evidence: verify-payment and the webhook both compute HMAC-SHA256 signatures using the server secret and validate incoming Razorpay payloads, which prevents trivial spoofing.
